summary: This Dockerfile creates a PHP development environment for running browser-based tests with Pest. It builds in two stages: first, a builder stage installs PHP, Node.js, Composer, and Playwright dependencies; then, a second stage copies everything over, sets up a non-root user for security, and starts a container that stays alive for development work.

explanations.3: This tells Docker to use a newer syntax version that supports advanced features like the cache mount we'll see later.
explanations.5: ARG lets you define build-time variables that can be passed in or overridden — this one sets which PHP CLI version to use as the base image.
explanations.15: This creates the first stage (named 'builder') starting from the PHP CLI image; the 'AS builder' part is important because we'll copy from it later.
explanations.17: We need to redeclare COMPOSER_VERSION here because ARG values don't carry over between stages — each stage starts fresh.
explanations.22: ENV sets environment variables that persist in the image; these tell npm and Playwright where to cache their files so they don't clutter the workspace.
explanations.26: The --mount=type=cache option tells Docker to use a temporary cache directory during the build that speeds up apt-get, then discards it after.
explanations.27: set -eux makes the script fail immediately on errors (-e), print commands as they run (-x), and treat undefined variables as errors (-u).
explanations.32: docker-php-ext-install is a helper that compiles and enables PHP extensions — zip and sockets in this case.
explanations.38: This pipes the Composer installer script directly to PHP with the --version flag to install a specific Composer version globally.
explanations.42: We create a minimal package.json to install Playwright — this is faster than installing from a full project file during build.
explanations.48: Similar to line 26, this caches Composer's vendor directory between builds so dependencies don't re-download every time.
explanations.54: This starts the final stage based on PHP-FPM (the FastCGI Process Manager for web servers) — we call it 'php' so we can reference it.
explanations.57: ENV TZ sets the timezone; the ${TIMEZONE} syntax substitutes the ARG value we passed in.
explanations.73: We redeclare these ARGs because, like COMPOSER_VERSION, they don't carry between stages.
explanations.77: set -e -x is similar to line 27 but -e stops on error and -x shows commands; this ensures user creation doesn't silently fail.
explanations.78: groupadd creates a system group that we'll use for the new user — the --gid flag sets its numeric ID.
explanations.79: useradd creates a new non-root user with specific permissions and a home directory; running as non-root is a security best practice.
explanations.84: COPY --from=builder copies everything we built in the first stage into this final stage; --chown changes ownership so our new user can access it.
explanations.89: We add node_modules/.bin to PATH so npm scripts and CLI tools are accessible anywhere in the shell.
explanations.92: USER switches the container to run commands as the non-root user from now on — this is a security measure.
explanations.95: npx (Node Package Executor) runs Playwright's install script to download the Chromium browser binary for testing.
explanations.98: ENTRYPOINT keeps the container running indefinitely by tailing /dev/null, useful for a dev container you can shell into.
